span.label: **TWO RIVAL MECHANISMS, TWENTY YEARS APART, STATED AS ALTERNATIVES:** `Quotation withheld.` **One says the concept got stronger; the other says the subject remembers what they did.** They are not degrees of the same account - one is about the representation and the other about the act - and until this paper the literature had been arguing which
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE ANSWER IS NEITHER - IT IS BOTH, SPLIT BY CONTENT:** `Quotation withheld.` **A dissociation inside a phenomenon the field had treated as one thing**, told apart only by varying the material while holding the task constant. This is the corpus's own thesis arriving as somebody else's empirical result: one term, two mechanisms, and no way to see it without the manipulation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **THE DESIGN POINT IS THE SAME ONE erb2019 MAKES, ONE RECORD APART:** `Quotation withheld.` The earlier literature compared mechanisms across experiments differing in more than the variable of interest. **Two consecutive records now say a body of results is uninterpretable because a confound was not held constant** - erb2019 about associative-priming overlap, this about task differences - and neither is a critique paper. Both are ordinary empirical papers that had to clear the ground before they could ask anything
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE ASYMMETRY IS EXPLAINED RATHER THAN NAMED - A CATEGORY HAS A LABEL AND A SYNONYM PAIR DOES NOT.** Evaluating whether roses and carnations share a category activates `flower`, and the next trial repeats that same evaluation against that same label; but `Quotation withheld.` **There is no operation to repeat, so only strengthening is left.** The mechanism is derived from the structure of the material rather than fitted to the result, which is what makes it a prediction for the next study rather than a description of this one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: semantic memory representations —causes→ long-term semantic priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — **ONE OF TWO MECHANISMS, AND THE EDGE IS ONLY TRUE IN ONE CONTENT DOMAIN.** The quote says `Long-term semantic priming OF WORD MEANINGS was dependent on` this - not long-term priming generally. Read alone this edge overstates; read with its twin below it is the paper's finding. **Q-804's `moderates` gap again**: the content domain conditions which mechanism applies and there is no way to say so on an edge, so it is said in the note and quoted whole in the second sense. Weight 0.9.

span.label: memory for prior cognitive operations —causes→ long-term semantic priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE OTHER MECHANISM, on the same sentence and at the same weight, and the pair is the point. This one holds for CATEGORY MEMBERSHIP only - and the fourth sense explains why, from the structure of the material: a category has a label that the same evaluation is repeated against, and a synonym pair has nothing to repeat. **Recording either edge without the other would turn a dissociation into a claim about the phenomenon as a whole**, which is the thing this paper exists to refute.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

Weight 0.95: the contrast is explicit in the quote and it is the paper's whole design.

span.label: Across two structurally matched experiments, long-term semantic priming turned out to rest on different memory processes depending on the kind of semantic content being processed.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming of word meanings rested on strengthened abstract semantic representations, whereas priming of category membership rested on memory for the cognitive operations performed earlier.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the category experiment, facilitation was larger when the prime trial required the same evaluation (exemplar or feature) as the target trial.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Category priming survived, though reduced, when prime and target operations differed, indicating a general rise in availability of category information on top of the operation-specific component.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the word-meaning experiment, matching versus mismatching the synonym/antonym evaluation across prime and target made no difference to the size of priming.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Both experiments produced priming that outlasted an average of seven unrelated intervening trials, with no content words shared between prime and target.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Priming measured in response rate was larger for category comparisons than for word-meaning comparisons.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Splitting Experiment 1 into halves showed priming did not grow across the session, so deliberate rehearsal or expectancy strategies do not explain the effects.
